objects.taxonomy_description: Cylindrical stick of wax (15-30 cm tall, 2-5 cm diameter) with a central wick (cotton string) extending from the top. The wax body is smooth and uniform, available in white, ivory, or colored varieties. The surface has a matte or slightly glossy finish depending on wax type (paraffin, beeswax, soy). The top has a charred wick tip if previously burned. Taper candles narrow toward the top; pillar candles maintain uniform diameter. The base is flat for standing. Scented candles may have a slightly textured surface from fragrance oils. The overall shape is a simple vertical cylinder with a thin wick protruding from the center.

objects.taxonomy_description: Domestic cat with a distinctive grey or tawny coat mottled with black in a tabby pattern. Coat features characteristic M-shaped marking on the forehead, dark stripes along the body, and ringed tail. Pattern types include classic (swirled), mackerel (striped), spotted, or ticked. Body is medium-sized, well-proportioned, and muscular. Head is round with a short muzzle. Ears are medium-sized, pointed, and erect. Eyes are large, round, and green, gold, or copper. The breed's signature features include the distinctive tabby pattern with M forehead marking and striped legs.

objects.taxonomy_description: Composite flower with a central yellow disc surrounded by a single whorl of white ray petals (florets). The flower head measures 2-5 cm in diameter with 13-34 elongated white petals radiating outward from the bright yellow center. The petals are narrow, slightly pointed, and arranged in a flat, circular pattern. The flower is supported by a slender green stem with small alternate leaves. The center disc has a bumpy, granular texture from individual disc florets.
